git status --short | head; git rev-parse HEAD; ls .shop/work/i39; ls runs 2>/dev/null | head; git log --oneline b4c4ad5e..HEAD | wc -l

cd .shop/work/i39; for f in w202.md w205.md w206.md requests.md supervision.md work-queue.md spec-integration.md design-model-check.md ledger.md; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done; ls runs; ls runs/w202 runs/w206

cat pytest.ini; /usr/bin/time -f "wall %e s" python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider > /tmp/i39-br3-suite.txt 2>&1; tail -30 /tmp/i39-br3-suite.txt
time python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rfEx 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning\|warnings\|^  \|^$" | tail -40

for w in w202 w205 w206; do echo "== $w"; python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --disable-warnings -p work_items --work-item $w 2>&1 | tail -1; done; echo "== w206 whole"; python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --disable-warnings -p work_items --work-item w206 --whole-suite 2>&1 | tail -1

result:
I reviewed i39 from its base to `ba907c58` and the outcome is **DONE_WITH_CONCERNS**: two findings in w206 need fixing now, and one check from the earlier reviews still can't be verified.

**Suite:** `Suite: 965 passed, 16 failed at ba907c58 in 26.42 s`. It runs in parallel and drives `scripts/work` as a subprocess rather than in-process. The 16 failures are the same scenarios as in review 2: they have scenarios but no work-item yet. With `--work-item w206 --whole-suite`, those 16 count as expected failures and nothing fails.

**Checks:** each work-item's tests pass (w202: 148, w205: 154, w206: 154). w206's four new unit tests pass. `tools size` prints nothing, every binding names a scenario, and no deprecated scenario is due for removal. Ruff reports 28 errors; the only new ones are two false positives in w206's code, and the rest were already there or come from helper scripts committed under `.shop/work/*/runs/`.

**Earlier findings:** w206 fixes review 2's two fix-now findings and its malformed `raised.jsonl` observation. No i39 work-item changed `features/`, and no test was removed or weakened.

**Fix now:**
1. **Merging has no spec line yet** (`scripts/supervise_change.py:79-89,108-111`). When a redraft round merges its ids into another proposal, no Behaviour line in the supervision spec covers it. The line exists only in request q20 (line 3), which is still open. The fix is to integrate that line, or to confirm that i39 closes with it carried by q20.
2. **The other proposal loses the pointer to its own drafts** (`scripts/supervise_change.py:112-115`). The merge also rewrites the other proposal's "The drafts of this proposal are in …" sentence to point at the redraft round's drafts. A probe confirmed it: an `approved` proposal not yet applied ended up pointing at another round's drafts. Its apply round would then work from those drafts, which don't hold its own lines, and replace its lists. i39's data is unharmed because every other proposal had already been applied. The fix is to leave that sentence alone when merging into another proposal; a matching test is written up in the findings.

**Can't verify (carried):** whether a real `claude -p` integrate round can read the upstream's spec outside its worktree (w202). Only a real session would show that.

The smaller observations are in the findings file. I changed nothing in the checkout, and the probe's scratch directory is deleted.

Files are in `.shop/scratch/branch-review/`:
- `findings.md`
- `result.json`
